ambiguities.evidence: The paper introduces Algorithm 1.1 only for nonsingular A and derives (4.1) by multiplying an expression containing A^{-1}; nevertheless, (4.1) itself contains no inverse. [PDF pp. 2, 7-8, printed A818 and A823-A824, Algorithm 1.1 and equations (3.7), (4.1)]
ambiguities.impact: A source-faithful formalization should retain nonsingularity as inherited paper context, while recognizing that the isolated algebraic lemma can validly be generalized to arbitrary conforming A. [PDF pp. 2 and 8, printed A818 and A824, Algorithm 1.1 and equation (4.1)]
ambiguities.issue: Nonsingularity is inherited from Algorithm 1.1 and from the derivation through (3.7), but is not algebraically needed for the final identity once (3.3) and (3.6) are assumed. [PDF pp. 2, 7-8, printed A818 and A823-A824, Algorithm 1.1 and equations (3.3), (3.6), (3.7), (4.1)]

contracts.contract_plain_english: One unscaled refinement step has an exact residual decomposition: the new signed residual equals the residual-computation error, plus the correction-equation defect, plus the update-rounding error after multiplication by A. Nothing in this passage alone bounds those terms or claims convergence. [PDF pp. 7-8, printed A823-A824, equations (3.3), (3.6), and (4.1)]

source_evidence.observation: For nonsingular A ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, Algorithm 1.1 computes the residual in precision u_r and rounds it to u_s, solves the correction equation in effective precision u_s while storing the correction in u, and forms the next iterate in u.

source_evidence.anchor: section 2, standard model and definition of γ_k
source_evidence.observation: The analysis adopts the standard floating-point model and defines γ_k = ku/(1−ku), with a superscript indicating which unit roundoff is used.
The computed residual and update are represented exactly as r̂_i = b−Ax̂_i+Δr_i and x̂_{i+1} = x̂_i+d̂_i+Δx_i, with stated componentwise bounds on Δr_i and Δx_i.
Multiplication of (3.7) by A gives the exact signed residual identity A x̂_{i+1}−b = Δr_i+A d̂_i−r̂_i+AΔx_i.
The rounding-error analysis explicitly ignores underflow and overflow; section 6 proposes a scaled algorithmic variant when these are a concern.

statement.algorithm_linkage: This is the exact one-step residual decomposition for the original, unscaled Algorithm 1.1: residual computation and rounding, correction solve, and precision-u update are linked without asserting convergence or stability. [PDF pp. 2, 7-8, printed A818 and A823-A824, Algorithm 1.1 and equations (3.3), (3.6), (4.1)]
binders: Let n be the system dimension, A ∈ ℝ^{n×n} be nonsingular, and b ∈ ℝ^n, as inherited from Algorithm 1.1. [PDF p. 2, printed A818, Algorithm 1.1]

For each loop index i ≥ 0, x̂_i and x̂_{i+1} are computed iterates, r̂_i is the computed-and-rounded residual, d̂_i is the computed correction, and Δr_i and Δx_i are their exact rounding-error terms. [PDF pp. 2 and 7, printed A818 and A823, Algorithm 1.1 and equations (3.3), (3.6)]
The unit roundoffs satisfy u_r ≤ u ≤ u_s ≤ u_f when the two precision-order statements are combined. [PDF pp. 1-2, printed A817-A818, equation (1.1) and the definition of u_s]
conclusions: For each i ≥ 0, A x̂_{i+1}−b = Δr_i+A d̂_i−r̂_i+AΔx_i exactly. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1)]
constants_and_indexing: The identity relates iteration i to i+1 and has no shifted residual other than r̂_i. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1)]
The update contribution is AΔx_i, not Δx_i, and the correction defect is A d̂_i−r̂_i with this sign. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1)]
The factors u_s, 1+u_s, and γ_p^r occur in the bound for Δr_i but not as explicit coefficients in the exact identity. [PDF pp. 7-8, printed A823-A824, equations (3.3) and (4.1)]
definitions_and_conventions: Δr_i is defined by r̂_i−(b−Ax̂_i), and Δx_i is defined by x̂_{i+1}−(x̂_i+d̂_i); they are exact error variables, not approximations or unspecified perturbations. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, equations (3.3) and (3.6)]
Absolute values of vectors and matrices are entrywise, and inequalities between vectors or matrices are componentwise. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, section 2 notation]

γ_p^r means pu_r/(1−pu_r), where p is the maximum number of nonzeros in a row of [A b], and p=n+1 for dense A and b. [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, definition of γ_k and text preceding equation (3.3)]
error_notions: The left side uses A x̂_{i+1}−b, the negative of the usual exact mathematical residual b−Ax̂_{i+1}; r̂_i is instead the residual actually computed and rounded during iteration i. [PDF pp. 7-8, printed A823-A824, equations (3.3) and (4.1)]
Equation (4.1) alone does not state a forward-error, normwise-backward-error, or componentwise-backward-error bound. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1) and the subsequent normwise analysis]
exceptional_values: The paper's analysis ignores underflow and overflow and therefore applies under the ordinary finite-value standard-model regime; the scaled replacement in section 6 is not part of this identity's Algorithm 1.1 linkage. [PDF p. 12, printed A828, section 6, Scaling]

The definition γ_p^r = pu_r/(1−pu_r) implicitly requires a nonzero, normally positive denominator for the stated finite bound. [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, definition of γ_k and use of γ_p^r]
higher_order_terms: No big-O or higher-order term is omitted from (4.1); all rounding effects are contained exactly in Δr_i and Δx_i. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1)]
The associated residual-error bound retains the factor 1+u_s rather than replacing it by a first-order approximation. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, equation (3.3)]
hypotheses: The computed residual has the exact representation r̂_i = b−Ax̂_i+Δr_i. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, equation (3.3)]
The computed update has the exact representation x̂_{i+1} = x̂_i+d̂_i+Δx_i. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, equation (3.6)]
The quantities are those produced by one iteration of the unscaled Algorithm 1.1. [PDF p. 2, printed A818, Algorithm 1.1]
implicit_context: A and b are treated as the precision-u input data, and all iterates are stored in precision u. [PDF pp. 1-2, printed A817-A818, precision definitions and Algorithm 1.1]
The paper obtains (4.1) by multiplying (3.7) by A, although the same identity follows directly from (3.3) and (3.6). [PDF pp. 7-8, printed A823-A824, equations (3.3), (3.6), (3.7), and (4.1)]

No solver-accuracy condition such as (2.3), (2.4), or (2.5) is invoked in the statement of the exact identity. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1) and the immediately following introduction of assumption (2.4)]
norms: No norm occurs in the identity itself. The surrounding rounding bounds use componentwise absolute values; infinity norms enter only in the subsequent analysis. [PDF pp. 7-8, printed A823-A824, equations (3.3), (3.6), and the text after (4.1)]
numerical_model: The residual error satisfies |Δr_i| ≤ u_s|b−Ax̂_i|+(1+u_s)γ_p^r(|b|+|A||x̂_i|). [PDF p. 7, printed A823, equation (3.3)]
The update error satisfies |Δx_i| ≤ u|x̂_{i+1}| under the cited variant of the standard rounding model. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, equation (3.6)]
Equation (4.1) itself is an exact algebraic identity after introducing these error variables; it is not a first-order approximation. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1)]

undebatable_constraints: The claimed equality is A x̂_{i+1}−b = Δr_i+A d̂_i−r̂_i+AΔx_i, with exactly the displayed signs and index offset. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1)]

All hatted vectors are computed quantities, whereas b−Ax̂_i is the exact residual of the stored iterate relative to the input A and b. [PDF pp. 2 and 7, printed A818 and A823, Algorithm 1.1 and equation (3.3)]
The result is one-step and exact; it contains no norm, inequality, convergence claim, or solver-stability premise. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1)]
Δr_i and Δx_i must remain distinct because they arise from different algorithmic operations and precisions. [PDF pp. 2 and 7, printed A818 and A823, Algorithm 1.1 and equations (3.3), (3.6)]

ambiguities.evidence: The preliminaries call c_1 and c_2 functions of n, A, r̂_i, and u_s, while Theorem 4.1 states one condition c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1 and then concludes the recurrence for every i≥0. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, solver-model explanation and Theorem 4.1]

[PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, equation (2.4) and Theorem 4.1]
ambiguities.issue: The theorem writes c_1 and c_2 without iteration subscripts even though the preliminaries allow them to depend on r̂_i. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, text after equations (2.3)-(2.5) and Theorem 4.1]

ambiguities.evidence: γ_p^r is defined with denominator 1−pu_r, but the theorem explicitly states only nonsingularity, (2.4), and c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, definition of γ_k and Theorem 4.1]
ambiguities.impact: A fully explicit formal statement must either assume pu_r<1 or bind γ_p^r abstractly together with the residual-error premise. [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, definition of γ_p^r and equation (3.3)]
ambiguities.issue: The standard-model smallness requirement needed for finite γ_p^r is implicit rather than included among Theorem 4.1's explicit hypotheses. [PDF pp. 5, 7, and 9, printed A821, A823, and A825, definition of γ_k, equation (3.3), and Theorem 4.1]

contracts.contract_plain_english: If every correction solve has the normwise residual quality prescribed by (2.4) and c_1κ∞(A)u_s is below one, then one refinement step satisfies an explicit infinity-norm residual recurrence. Its multiplicative coefficient contains the correction-solver instability, while its additive term contains residual-computation and update-rounding errors with all finite-precision factors retained. [PDF pp. 8-9, printed A824-A825, equation (4.1), displayed derivation, and Theorem 4.1]

source_evidence.observation: The theorem concerns the computed iterates of the unscaled mixed-precision iterative-refinement algorithm.
The paper defines κ∞(A)=‖A^{-1}‖∞‖A‖∞ and assumes a normwise correction-solver residual bound involving nonnegative quantities c_1 and c_2.
The residual-computation and update-rounding errors have the componentwise models later converted to infinity-norm bounds.
After defining h_i=r̂_i−A d̂_i, the paper applies (2.4) and bounds d̂_i through A^{-1}(r̂_i−h_i).

source_evidence.anchor: displayed derivation immediately before Theorem 4.1 and Theorem 4.1
source_evidence.observation: Under c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1, the correction defect is isolated and then substituted into (4.1), yielding the residual recurrence and the exact displayed definitions of α_i and β_i.
The analysis ignores underflow and overflow; scaling is proposed later as a modified algorithm.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The result bounds one unscaled Algorithm 1.1 step by combining the residual rounding model, the normwise correction-solver defect model (2.4), and the precision-u update model. [PDF pp. 2, 7-9, printed A818 and A823-A825, Algorithm 1.1, equations (2.4), (3.3), (3.6), (4.1), and Theorem 4.1]
binders: Let A ∈ ℝ^{n×n} be nonsingular and b ∈ ℝ^n, and let Algorithm 1.1 produce x̂_i, r̂_i, d̂_i, and x̂_{i+1} for i ≥ 0. [PDF pp. 2 and 9, printed A818 and A825, Algorithm 1.1 and Theorem 4.1]
Let c_1 and c_2 be the nonnegative solver-bound quantities from (2.4), and define h_i := r̂_i−A d̂_i. [PDF pp. 5 and 8, printed A821 and A824, equation (2.4) and the text after (4.1)]

Let κ∞(A):=‖A^{-1}‖∞‖A‖∞, let p be the maximum row nonzero count of [A b], and let γ_p^r:=pu_r/(1−pu_r). [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, equation (2.1), definition of γ_k, and text preceding (3.3)]
conclusions: The exact starting identity is A x̂_{i+1}−b=Δr_i+A d̂_i−r̂_i+AΔx_i. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1)]
The first correction-defect bound is ‖h_i‖∞ ≤ u_s(c_1‖A‖∞‖d̂_i‖∞+c_2‖r̂_i‖∞) ≤ u_s(c_1‖A‖∞‖A^{-1}‖∞(‖r̂_i‖∞+‖h_i‖∞)+c_2‖r̂_i‖∞). [PDF p. 8, printed A824, displayed h_i derivation]
Isolating h_i under c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1 gives ‖h_i‖∞ ≤ u_s[(c_1κ∞(A)+c_2)/(1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s)]‖r̂_i‖∞. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, first displayed bound]

Before eliminating r̂_i, the one-step residual bound is ‖b−Ax̂_{i+1}‖∞ ≤ u_s‖b−Ax̂_i‖∞+(1+u_s)γ_p^r(‖b‖∞+‖A‖∞‖x̂_i‖∞)+u_s[(c_1κ∞(A)+c_2)/(1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s)]‖r̂_i‖∞+u‖A‖∞‖x̂_{i+1}‖∞. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, first residual inequality before Theorem 4.1]
After a second use of (3.3), Theorem 4.1 concludes ‖b−Ax̂_{i+1}‖∞ ≤ α_i‖b−Ax̂_i‖∞+β_i for every i≥0. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, final displayed derivation and Theorem 4.1]
The coefficient is α_i=u_s(1+(1+u_s)(c_1κ∞(A)+c_2)/(1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s)). [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
The additive term is β_i=(1+u_s(c_1κ∞(A)+c_2)/(1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s))(1+u_s)γ_p^r(‖b‖∞+‖A‖∞‖x̂_i‖∞)+u‖A‖∞‖x̂_{i+1}‖∞. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
constants_and_indexing: The result is quantified for i≥0 and relates residual i+1 to residual i. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
The strict condition is c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1, and the same expression appears in the exact denominator 1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, defect bound and Theorem 4.1]
α_i contains the factor 1+u_s outside the correction-defect ratio, while β_i contains both 1+u_s and the separate update term involving x̂_{i+1}. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
The residual-rounding contribution in β_i uses x̂_i, whereas the update-rounding contribution uses x̂_{i+1}. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
definitions_and_conventions: h_i is the computed correction-equation residual r̂_i−A d̂_i, whereas b−Ax̂_i is the exact residual of the current stored iterate for the original system. [PDF pp. 8-9, printed A824-A825, text after (4.1) and Theorem 4.1]
c_1 and c_2 are nonnegative functions of n, A, r̂_i, and u_s according to the preliminary solver model. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, text following equations (2.3)-(2.5)]
γ_p^r=pu_r/(1−pu_r), with p the maximum number of nonzeros in a row of [A b]. [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, definition of γ_k and text preceding (3.3)]
error_notions: The recurrence controls the exact normwise residual ‖b−Ax̂_i‖∞ of the original system, not the computed residual norm ‖r̂_i‖∞. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
h_i measures the residual of the computed correction d̂_i in the correction equation A d=r̂_i. [PDF pp. 5 and 8, printed A821 and A824, equation (2.4) and definition of h_i]

Theorem 4.1 itself does not normalize the residual by ‖A‖∞‖x̂_i‖∞+‖b‖∞ and therefore does not by itself state a bound on the normwise relative backward error η. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, definition of η and Theorem 4.1]
exceptional_values: The strict denominator condition excludes 1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s≤0. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, assumption preceding the isolated h_i bound and Theorem 4.1]

The γ_p^r expression presupposes a finite standard-model bound, ordinarily pu_r<1; this side condition is not restated in Theorem 4.1. [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, definition and use of γ_p^r]
Underflow and overflow are ignored by this analysis; the later scaling modification is outside Theorem 4.1 as stated. [PDF p. 12, printed A828, section 6, Scaling]
higher_order_terms: Theorem 4.1 is stated with exact rational factors in u_s and does not use big-O or ≲ notation. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
Factors 1+u_s and the denominator 1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s are retained and must not be silently replaced by first-order approximations. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, displayed derivation and Theorem 4.1]
hypotheses: The solver used in step 4 satisfies ‖r̂_i−A d̂_i‖∞ ≤ u_s(c_1‖A‖∞‖d̂_i‖∞+c_2‖r̂_i‖∞). [PDF p. 5, printed A821, equation (2.4)]
The denominator condition c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1 holds. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, opening line of the derivation and Theorem 4.1]
The residual and update obey r̂_i=b−Ax̂_i+Δr_i with the bound in (3.3), and x̂_{i+1}=x̂_i+d̂_i+Δx_i with |Δx_i|≤u|x̂_{i+1}|. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, equations (3.3) and (3.6)]
The unit roundoffs inherit u_r≤u≤u_s≤u_f from the algorithm's precision ordering. [PDF pp. 1-2, printed A817-A818, equation (1.1) and the definition of u_s]
implicit_context: A and b are precision-u input data, residuals are computed at u_r and rounded to u_s, corrections are effectively solved at u_s and stored at u, and updates are performed at u. [PDF pp. 1-2, printed A817-A818, precision definitions and Algorithm 1.1]

Theorem 4.1 requires only solver condition (2.4), not the relative-forward-solve condition (2.3) or componentwise solver condition (2.5). [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, equations (2.3)-(2.5) and Theorem 4.1]

Although labeled α_i, its displayed formula depends on i only through any iteration dependence hidden in c_1 and c_2; β_i additionally contains x̂_i and x̂_{i+1}. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, text after equations (2.3)-(2.5) and Theorem 4.1]
norms: Every norm in the theorem and its displayed derivation is the vector or induced matrix infinity norm. [PDF pp. 8-9, printed A824-A825, h_i derivation and Theorem 4.1]
The passage uses κ∞(A), not a two-norm condition number or the componentwise condition number cond(A). [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, equation (2.1) and Theorem 4.1]

Residual computation contributes the γ_p^r term and residual rounding contributes factors involving u_s; update rounding contributes u‖A‖∞‖x̂_{i+1}‖∞. [PDF pp. 7 and 9, printed A823 and A825, equations (3.3), (3.6), and Theorem 4.1]

contracts.contract_plain_english: Under a componentwise correction-solver defect bound and the uniform one-half condition (5.6), a nonnegative M-matrix resolvent controls the correction contribution and yields an exact componentwise recurrence for the next true residual. The theorem includes a nonnegative additive vector y_i; only the subsequent first-order interpretation gives the approximate infinity-norm estimate (5.7), and the theorem alone does not yet bound ω. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, equations (5.2)-(5.7) and Theorem 5.1]

source_evidence.observation: The paper defines cond(A), assumes the componentwise correction-solver residual bound |r̂_i−A d̂_i|≤u_sG_i|d̂_i|, and defines componentwise relative backward error ω.
For the componentwise backward-error quotient, ξ/0 is interpreted as zero when ξ=0 and as infinity otherwise.
The residual and update rounding models used in section 5 are stated componentwise.

The paper derives the base componentwise residual inequality, defines Z_1 and the M-matrix inverse M_1, proves its nonnegativity and norm bound under a one-half condition, and states the theorem's uniform hypothesis.
The theorem gives the componentwise residual recurrence with W_i and y_i, followed by a first-order interpretation of W_i and its infinity-norm bound.
The analysis ignores underflow and overflow; a scaled modification is proposed separately.
